To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the FBS0 fertilizer increased the percentage and the proportion of ARS producing bacteria in the rhizospheres of durum wheat crops grown on soils with low Olsen P content.

the application of a fertilizer granule containing elemental sulfur (FBS0), in durum wheat crops, substantially improved the quality and the dynamics of the soil's rhizosphere at the available phosphorous limiting level by modically the abundance of the rhizosphere bacterial communities, thus effectively enhancing the microbe mediated nutrient mobilization, towards improved plant nutritional status.

the application of FBS0 improved the rhizosphere's bacterial community structure, which was reflected by a significant increase of ARS producing bacteria and an enhanced release of organic S, thus improving the soil's quality and the plant's nutrition.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new type of fertilizer granules, which could be used in the cultivation of cereal crops on soils with low available phosphorus levels, thus improving crop yield and quality, and reducing the use of chemical fertilizers.
the effect of Fertilizers containing Elemental Sulfur (S0), on the rhizospherically active bacteria of a durum wheat crop, cultivated on a calcareous soil, with Olsen P content of 7.8-16.8 mg P kg 1.
the development of an environmentally sustainable fertilizer formulation, which can be used in a conventional way and improve the soil quality and plant nutritional dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of FBS0 in durum wheat crops is a feasible practice, which could be adopted in the Mediterranean region.

the use of FBS0, at the tested level, is a viable and effective strategy to enhance the yield of durum wheat crop in a P deficient soil, by improving the rhizosoils' quality and the plant nutritional dynamics.

the FBS0 application, in the presence of a low Olsen P soil, enhanced the rhizospherical microbial communities and improved the nutrient balance of the crop, which in turn resulted in a higher yield compared to the conventional F treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of FBS0 as a fertilizer in durum wheat crop, under conditions where Olsen P is below 8 mg kg-1, can be considered a sustainable agricultural practice, since the crop's yield was comparable to the conventional one, while the rhizospherically active bacterial communities were substantially improved.
the FBS0 application, in addition to improving the soil fertility, also improved the plant nutrition, and thus the yield, of a wheat crop cultivated in a calcareous soil with low Olsen P content.

the FBS0 fertilizer application, in the presence of available P, increased the yield of durum wheat, by enhancing the rhizospherical microbial community's ability to mobilize the nutrients, which are essential for the plant's development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of S0 as a component of the fertilizers can be an effective tool to improve crop production, particularly in soils with low available phosphorus.
the use of FBS0 is an effective and sustainable approach to improve the soil fertility and crop quality in arid and semi-arid regions with calcareous soils and limited available phosphorus.
the application of FBS0 can be an effective tool to improve the quality of marginal soils with a low available P content, while maintaining a high yield.
